chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ribat, from one who narrated it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"If a defect occurs in the animal before three days, it belongs to the seller."

key_terms.حَدَث: Occurrence/Defect (specifically a hidden flaw or disease)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on animal defects appearing within three days of sale in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* codifies the 'three-day defect period' (khalq al-thalathah) in animal sales, a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence that shifts liability to the seller for latent defects emerging shortly after the transaction. It reflects the practical concern for animal welfare and market fairness, ensuring buyers are not burdened with pre-existing or early-onset ailments that were not apparent at the time of sale.
